steps.title: What do you want Hermes to do for you?
steps.rail_subtitle: What you want Hermes to do
steps.intro: Hermes is an AI agent: an AI that can do things for you, not only talk. You talk to it in plain words, as you would with ChatGPT. The difference is what it can do around the chat. It can take actions on the computer it runs on, it remembers you from one chat to the next, and it can work on a schedule or answer you in a chat app on your phone. What you want from it decides which of these parts you need, so this is the first question. Pick the answer closest to yours. You can change it later.

intro_sources.quote: builds a deepening model of who you are across sessions
Tools are functions that extend the agent's capabilities.
The gateway is a single background process that connects to all your configured platforms, handles sessions, runs cron jobs

facts.text: Hermes remembers what it learns about you from one chat to the next. It also writes down new skills (step-by-step know-how for one kind of task) from what it does, and improves them as it uses them.
facts.quote: creates skills from experience, improves them during use, nudges itself to persist knowledge, and builds a deepening model of who you are across sessions

facts.text: Hermes can take actions, not only answer: run programs, read and change files, search the web, and more. Each kind of action is called a tool.
facts.quote: covering web search, browser automation, terminal execution, file editing, memory, delegation, scheduled tasks, and more

facts.text: You can message Hermes from chat apps such as Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord or Slack, not only from this app. A part of Hermes called the gateway keeps running in the background to answer you there.
facts.quote: The gateway is a single background process that connects to all your configured platforms

facts.text: Hermes can do jobs on a schedule without you being there, such as a summary every morning or a regular check. The docs call these cron jobs.
facts.quote: Cron jobs let Hermes Agent run tasks on a schedule — daily summaries, periodic checks, automated reports — without you being present.

facts.text: The official docs sort what people do with Hermes into a few kinds: help with writing and running code, a bot in a chat app, jobs that run on a schedule, and a team of specialist bots. They advise getting one plain chat working first, then adding one thing at a time.
facts.quote: I want a team of specialist Bots

more_sources.quote: Get one clean conversation working first, then layer on gateway, cron, skills, voice, or routing.

steps.title: The brain: what a model is, and where it runs
steps.rail_subtitle: What a model is, where it runs
steps.intro: Hermes doesn't think by itself. It sends your words to a model: the AI that does the thinking, like the one inside ChatGPT. A provider is the company that runs a model for you. If Hermes already answers you, you already have a model, and this step shows what you have and what else you could use. There are four ways to connect a model: a subscription you may already pay for, an API key (a secret code from a model company), a model on your own computer, or a Nous account (Nous Research makes Hermes). You can switch at any time.

intro_sources.quote: Main model — what the agent thinks with.

intro_sources.section: Subscription plans: what your plan pays for
intro_sources.quote: Several providers let you sign in to Hermes with a consumer subscription
You can switch providers at any time with hermes model — no lock-in.

left.title: On a provider's computers
left.text: Your words go to that provider and nowhere else. You pay through a subscription or for what you use.
left.quote: API calls go only to the LLM provider you configure

right.title: On this computer
right.text: Nothing leaves your computer, and it costs nothing to run. It needs a fairly strong computer.
right.quote: Nothing leaves your computer: no account, no API key, and no network access

facts.text: The name of the model you use shows in the message box, and you can change it there for one chat. The model for new chats is set in Settings, then Model, then Main model, and you can switch to another one at any time.
facts.quote: Set the default in Settings → Model → Main model.

facts.text: Some subscriptions can be used instead of a key: a ChatGPT plan (you sign in with ChatGPT) or SuperGrok (the paid plan for Grok). For Claude, only the Max plan works, and only with extra usage credits bought on top; Claude Pro can't be used this way. The docs name ChatGPT Plus and Pro, but don't yet say how much of your plan Hermes uses.
facts.section: Subscription plans: what your plan pays for
facts.quote: Pro subscribers cannot use the OAuth path

more_sources.section: Subscription plans: what your plan pays for
more_sources.quote: Which ChatGPT plan tiers are eligible, and how Hermes usage counts against your plan's Codex limits, are not currently documented
Using Codex OAuth (ChatGPT Pro/Plus account — no API key needed)

facts.text: An API key is a long secret code from a model company, such as OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic or Google. It works like a password that lets Hermes use your account there, and you usually pay for what you use. Keep it secret: it goes in Settings, then Providers, then API keys, never into a chat.
facts.quote: or API key for pay-per-token

more_sources.quote: You pay only for the LLM API usage from your chosen provider.
with an Accounts / API-keys UX for signing in and storing credentials per provider

facts.text: Hermes can download a model and run it on this computer: no account, no key, and nothing leaves your computer. A graphics card with 8 GB of memory or more runs the small models well, and Hermes shows which models fit before you download. Small models sometimes say they saved something to Hermes's memory when they didn't.
facts.quote: A GPU with 8 GB+ of memory runs the small catalog models comfortably

more_sources.section: How Hermes picks what to download
more_sources.quote: Every model in the catalog is priced against your machine before you download anything.
Small local models (roughly under 30B parameters) and models with weak tool-calling do this often

facts.text: Nous Portal is an account with Nous Research, the makers of Hermes. One sign-in gives you hundreds of models and extra tools such as web search, on a paid subscription, and the docs call it the recommended way to run Hermes. There is also a free Nous plan, with limits on how much you can use it.
facts.quote: the recommended way to run Hermes Agent

more_sources.quote: One OAuth login covers 300+ frontier agentic models
on the free Nous tier (no sign-in)

steps.title: Where Hermes runs: this computer, or one that is always on
steps.rail_subtitle: This computer, or one that is always on
steps.intro: Hermes itself also runs on a computer, and that is a separate choice from the model in step 2. By default, this app runs Hermes on this computer. Hermes can also run on another computer that stays on all the time, and this app then connects to it. Where Hermes runs decides when it can work for you. Answering your messages and running scheduled jobs happen in the background on that computer, so they need it to be on and awake.

intro_sources.quote: By default the app starts and manages its own local backend.
The gateway is a single background process that connects to all your configured platforms, handles sessions, runs cron jobs
stops the machine from sleeping so long or overnight agent runs keep going

left.title: This computer
left.text: Simplest: nothing extra to set up. It works only while this computer is on and awake.
left.quote: By default the app starts and manages its own local backend.

right.title: A computer that is always on
right.text: A rented server, a home server, or Hermes Cloud. It keeps working while your own computer is off.
right.quote: a VPS, a home server, or a Mini behind Tailscale

facts.text: By default, the app starts and looks after its own Hermes on this computer. Nothing else is needed to begin.
facts.quote: By default the app starts and manages its own local backend.

facts.text: Hermes works only while the computer it runs on is awake. In the app, Settings, then Advanced, then Keep computer awake stops the computer from sleeping during long jobs. Closing the lid still puts it to sleep.
facts.quote: Closing the lid or choosing Sleep still sleeps the machine

more_sources.quote: Scheduled fires work as long as the gateway is running

facts.text: Hermes can also run on another computer that stays on, such as a server you rent (a computer in a data centre that stays on) or one at home. You connect this app to it in Settings, then Gateways, and use it the same way. Setting up that other computer takes some technical steps with typed commands.
facts.quote: point it at a Hermes backend running on another machine — a VPS, a home server, or a Mini behind Tailscale

more_sources.quote: Set a username and password, then start the backend bound to a reachable address.

facts.text: Hermes Cloud runs Hermes for you on a computer that is hosted for you. You sign in once in Settings, then Gateways, and pick your Hermes from a list, with no address to type in. The Hermes docs don't list its price.
facts.quote: sign in once to Hermes Cloud and pick from the agents on your account; no URL to paste

more_sources.quote: A hosted instance discovered through your Hermes Cloud account.

facts.text: Your chats, memory and skills are kept on the computer where Hermes runs. Hermes sends your words only to your model's provider, and it collects no usage data.
facts.quote: Hermes Agent does not collect telemetry, usage data, or analytics. Your conversations, memory, and skills are stored locally in ~/.hermes/.

options.label: This computer is fine for now
A computer that is always on

steps.title: Connecting things: tools, skills, plugins, MCP
steps.intro: Hermes does things through tools: actions it can take, like searching the web. You can give it more abilities in three ways: skills, plugins and MCP. The names sound alike, but they are different kinds of things. Knowing which kind fits your goal tells you what to ask your Hermes for. This page explains and advises. Your own Hermes does the adding, after you say yes.

intro_sources.quote: Tools are functions that extend the agent's capabilities.

intro_sources.section: I want to build custom tools/skills
intro_sources.quote: Extend Hermes Agent with your own tools and reusable skill packages.

facts.text: A tool is one kind of action Hermes can take, such as searching the web, running a program or reading a file. Hermes comes with many, grouped into toolsets that you can switch on or off.
facts.quote: They're organized into logical toolsets that can be enabled or disabled per platform.

facts.text: A skill is written know-how: a document with step-by-step instructions for one kind of task. Hermes reads only each skill's short description until a task needs it, so having many doesn't slow it down. It comes with many skills, and you can add more from the Skills Hub.
facts.quote: The agent reads the short descriptions for free and only loads a skill's full content when a task actually calls for it

more_sources.quote: Skills are on-demand knowledge documents the agent can load when needed.

facts.text: A plugin is an add-on made of code. It can give Hermes new tools or features without changing Hermes itself. The plugin catalog lists plugins that people have reviewed, and each one installs with one command or one click.
facts.quote: Hermes has a plugin system for adding custom tools, hooks, and integrations without modifying core code.

more_sources.quote: The plugin catalog is a curated, human-reviewed directory of Hermes plugins you can install by name with a single command

facts.text: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a shared standard, a bit like a plug that fits many sockets. It lets Hermes use tools that live outside it, such as GitHub or a database, without anyone writing a new Hermes tool first.
facts.quote: Access to external tool ecosystems without writing a native Hermes tool first

more_sources.quote: MCP lets Hermes Agent connect to external tool servers so the agent can use tools that live outside Hermes itself — GitHub, databases

facts.text: Add only what your goal needs, one thing at a time. The official quickstart says to get a normal chat working first, then add skills, scheduled jobs or messaging one layer at a time.
facts.quote: Get one clean conversation working first, then layer on gateway, cron, skills, voice, or routing.
